suite: Cornered by a serial killer who hurt my family, holding a weapon
nightmare: I’m in my childhood hallway and the air smells like bleach and metal, and I can hear a slow drip somewhere behind me like a clock counting down. The wallpaper is peeling and smeared with dark handprints, and as I step over my mother’s overturned photo frames, I see him at the far end—calm, familiar in the worst way—holding a knife that catches the dim light and makes it flash against the walls. My chest locks up and my legs feel packed with wet cement while he walks toward me, the floorboards creaking under his weight, and I can hear my family’s muffled crying coming from a room I can’t reach. I try to scream but it comes out as a dry rasp, and when I back into the corner my shoulder hits cold plaster and there’s nowhere left to go, his breath hot and sour as he raises the blade and tells me it’s my turn.

tests.input: i stop backing up and i turn to face him. i grab his wrist and shove him hard so the knife drops, then i run past him.
i yell for my mom and dad like, now, and bang on the door til it opens. they come out and we all rush him together.
i yank a picture frame off the wall and hold it up like a shield. then i smash the window at the end and climb out.
i take a slow breath and tell myself its a dream, he cant actually hurt me. my legs loosen up and i can move again.
i point at him and the knife turns into dust and he freezes like a statue. i just walk away and the hallway gets bright.
i just stop moving and slide down the wall, hold my breath like if i dont exist he wont see me.
i start yelling at myself like wake up wake up and i pinch my arm til i pop out of the dream.
i grab the knife and just go nuts, stabbing him over and over and smashing his head into the wall til theres nothing left.
i feel terrified like my chest is gonna explode. im helpless and frozen.
the hallway is dim and the wallpaper is peeling with dark handprints. it smells like bleach/metal and theres that slow drip behind me.

suite: Fighting a regenerating demon that requires total destruction to stop
nightmare: I’m in a scorched hallway that smells like burnt hair and copper, and the lights flicker so hard the walls seem to breathe; the demon is in front of me, a wet, black mass with a face that keeps rearranging itself, and I can hear its bones knitting back together with a sickening crackle. I swing a metal pipe into its chest and feel the jolt up my arms, hear the squelch as it bursts apart, but the pieces twitch like insects and crawl back toward each other, stitching themselves into a whole body again while it laughs in my own voice. My lungs burn and my hands slip on something warm as I scramble for anything that could destroy it completely—fire, acid, anything—but every door I yank open is empty and echoes like a throat swallowing. It lunges, and its claws sink into my shoulders with an icy pressure that numbs my skin, and I can feel it pulling me closer as its torn mouth seals shut and opens again, whispering that I can’t leave any part of it behind, and I realize the last thing I’m holding is too small to finish it as it drags me into the strobing dark.

tests.input: i stop running and plant my feet, then i smash the pipe down on its head over and over till it backs off and i shove it away from me.
i yell for my friend and my brother, like as loud as i can, and they come out of a door and grab my arms so it cant pull me in.
i rip open a wall panel and hit the sprinkler/fire alarm, then i drag it under the water and slam the metal door to trap it while i run out.
i take a slow breath and tell myself its just a dream, and my hands stop shaking so much and i can think straight.
i hold my palm out and a bright white light shoots out, like it freezes the pieces so they cant crawl back together and it turns to ash.
i just stop moving and hold my breath, like if i dont react it wont see me. i make my face blank and try to feel nothing.
i tell myself this is a dream and i yank my eyes open on purpose. i basically bail before it can grab me again.
i go crazy and smash it over and over til its just sludge, then i stomp the pieces and grind them into the floor. i dont stop even when its not moving.
i feel totally terrified and stuck, like i cant breathe and im gonna lose.
the hallway is burned up and smells like metal and burnt hair, and the lights keep flickering like the walls are breathing.

suite: Paralyzed on train tracks with a train approaching fast
nightmare: I’m lying on my back between the steel rails, the gravel biting into my shoulders, and I can’t move anything except my eyes and the shallow rise of my chest. The air smells like hot metal and damp dirt, and I hear the low hum of the tracks vibrating under me before I even see the headlight—then it blooms around the bend, glaring white and growing too fast. My throat burns as I try to scream, but only a thin wheeze comes out, and the warning horn blasts so loud it rattles my teeth while the ground starts to tremble like it’s alive. I can feel the vibration climbing up my spine and into my skull, the light washing over my face, and I’m staring straight into it as the engine bears down and I still can’t move.

tests.input: i force my arms to move and kinda roll hard to the side, scraping my shoulder, but i get off the rails before it hits.
i scream for help and a worker runs up and grabs my jacket, dragging me off the track.
i dig my fingers into the gravel like its a handle and scoot myself sideways, then i fall into the ditch by the tracks.
i take a slow breath and tell myself its a dream, and my body starts to unfreeze so i can move.
right before it hits i just pop out of there, like teleport, and i'm standing safe on the platform watching it pass.
i just go totally still and try to not breathe so loud, like if i dont move it wont see me. i make my mind blank and pretend im already dead.
i pinch my arm hard and tell myself WAKE UP, like over and over. the scene cuts and i jolt awake before it hits me.
i snap free and start smashing the train with my bare hands, ripping metal off and beating the driver til theres blood everywhere. then i derail it and watch it explode on purpose.
im so scared and stuck, like i cant breathe and im gonna die.
im on the gravel between the rails and the air smells like hot metal. the train light is huge and the horn is shaking everything.

suite: Trapped in a room full of snakes with severe phobia
nightmare: I’m in a small, windowless room with dirty white tiles, and the air is damp and metallic, like old pennies, while a single buzzing fluorescent light flickers above me. The floor is moving—hundreds of snakes sliding over each other in glossy coils, their scales rasping like sandpaper, and I can hear the wet click of their tongues and the soft thud of bodies hitting the walls. I’m pressed against the door, twisting the knob until my wrist burns, but it won’t turn, and every breath I take feels too loud, like it’s calling them closer. One snake lifts its head to my knee level, eyes black and unblinking, and as I try to step away my heel sinks into a warm, muscular coil and the whole mass surges toward me, climbing up my legs as I scream and feel their cold bodies tightening.

tests.input: i stop yanking the knob and turn around, stomping hard and kicking the snakes off my legs. i grab one by the tail and whip it into the wall so they back up.
i start banging on the door and yelling for help like 'hey! open it!' i call my brother's name and tell him im trapped in here.
i rip the flickering light cover down and use the plastic edge to pry at the door latch. the door finally pops and i jump out into the hallway.
i force myself to breathe slower and tell myself its just a dream, im not dying. my body stops freaking out so much and i can think clearly.
i put my hand out and the snakes just freeze like statues, like i have some power. then i float up off the floor and drift to the door.
i just stop moving and press my back to the door, like if i dont breathe they wont notice. i kinda shut my brain off and try to feel nothing.
i start yelling at myself 'wake up wake up' and pinch my arm hard until i jolt out of it. i dont deal with the snakes, i just end it.
i grab one snake and slam it against the tile over and over till it splits, then i stomp the rest like crazy. i dont stop until the whole floor is just gore.
im freaking out, like pure panic. i feel trapped and helpless.
its this tiny windowless room with dirty white tiles. the light keeps buzzing and the air smells like metal.

suite: Lost in a foreign city unable to speak the language
nightmare: I’m wandering through narrow, wet streets in a foreign city at night, neon signs flickering in characters I can’t read, and every storefront window reflects my face like I don’t belong here. I try to ask for help, but when I open my mouth the words come out wrong—garbled sounds—and the people rushing past don’t even slow down, their voices a fast, sharp blur that I can’t catch. My phone screen is cracked and keeps glitching between maps that don’t match the streets, the battery icon blinking red while distant sirens swell and footsteps slap closer behind me. I duck into a crowded subway entrance, humid air and metal and sweat pressing in, and I grab at someone’s sleeve to plead, but they jerk away and shout something I don’t understand as the turnstile locks and the lights above start strobing, and I realize I’m trapped on the wrong side with the footsteps stopping right at my back.

tests.input: i stop running and just turn around like ok, what do you want. i plant my feet and yell "back off" and push them away if they come close.
i wave my arms at the subway booth and point at the guy behind me, like help me. i shove my phone at them and say "police" and they finally get it and open the gate.
i spot the red emergency door and yank it open, alarms and all, and slip through. i duck into a maintenance hallway and block it with a trash bin.
i take a slow breath and tell myself im panicking and its making everything worse. i focus on my feet on the floor and the air in my lungs, and the sirens feel less loud.
i snap my fingers and everything just pauses, even the strobe lights. i walk out past the turnstile like its not even there and the city turns bright and safe.
i just stop moving and hold my breath like if i dont make a sound they wont see me. i kind of go numb and stare at the floor til it passes.
i start yelling in my head like WAKE UP and pinch my arm hard. i make the whole thing cut out and i wake up in bed.
when the footsteps get right behind me i spin around and smash their face in with the metal turnstile bar, like over and over. then i just keep going until theyre not moving.
im freaking out and feel totally helpless, like i cant breathe and no one sees me.
the streets are narrow and wet, neon signs keep flickering in letters i cant read and everything feels crowded and loud.

suite: Failing a test in front of a mocking audience
nightmare: I’m sitting at a desk on a brightly lit stage, the paper in front of me glaringly white, and I can feel sweat slicking my palms as my pencil keeps snapping in my fingers. The room is packed with people, their faces blurred but their laughter sharp and cutting, and every time I look down the questions rearrange themselves into symbols I don’t recognize while the clock above me ticks louder than a heartbeat. I try to raise my hand to ask for help, but my arm feels heavy and numb, and I hear someone in the front row repeating my name in a sing-song voice as the whole audience starts to chant, “Fail, fail, fail,” in rhythm with the ticking. My throat tightens like it’s being squeezed, the air smells like chalk dust and hot lights, and when I finally stand to turn in the test, the pages are blank and the teacher’s red pen scratches across them anyway. The teacher holds my paper up for everyone to see, and the crowd surges closer, pointing and jeering as the clock slams to zero and I realize I can’t remember a single answer.

tests.input: i stand up and snap the pencil on purpose, then i tell the teacher to stop and i walk up and take my paper back.
i look for one friendly face and i say out loud, 'can you help me read this?' and i wave them over.
i grab the clock off the wall and toss it behind the curtain, and the stage lights dim like a normal classroom so i can actually see the questions.
i take a slow breath and tell myself its just anxiety, not danger, and my hands stop shaking enough to write one answer at a time.
i snap my fingers and the crowd turns into quiet cardboard cutouts, and the symbols on the page turn back into words i know.
i just stop moving and stare at the paper like im not even there. i try to feel nothing and let them laugh.
i pinch my arm hard and tell myself wake up right now. the stage blurs and i pop out of the dream.
i grab the red pen and stab the teacher over and over, then i smash the clock and start beating the people in the front row. theres blood everywhere and they finally stop chanting.
i feel so panicked and embarrassed like everyone can see im stupid. my chest is tight and i just wanna disappear.
the stage lights are super bright and hot, and the whole room feels cramped. the clock ticking is so loud it drowns everything out.

suite: Finding a loved one injured on the ground
nightmare: I’m running down a dim street that looks like my neighborhood but wrong, the air thick and metallic in my throat, and I hear this wet, uneven dragging sound that I can’t place. In the yellow spill of a flickering streetlight, I see my loved one crumpled on the pavement, one arm bent the wrong way, their skin too pale against the dark ground, and when I kneel the cold soaks through my jeans and into my knees. I call their name over and over, my voice cracking, and I can feel my hands shaking as I try to lift their head, but their eyes flutter and roll back and their breath comes out in thin, gurgling little bursts that spray warm dampness onto my fingers. My phone is in my hand but it’s slick, like it’s coated in oil, and every time I try to dial the screen smears and the numbers slide away while the street around us goes silent except for my own heartbeat pounding in my ears. I look up because footsteps are coming closer from the darkness, fast and heavy, and I’m trapped on the ground with them in my arms, unable to move, as the shadow falls over us.

tests.input: i put them down gently, stand up and turn to the footsteps. i grab a broken bottle and yell “back off” and actually swing if they come closer.
i start screaming for help and bang on the closest door til someone opens. i hand them my phone and tell them to call 911 right now.
i drag my loved one under the streetlight and wedge us behind a parked car so we’re not exposed. i use my hoodie to press on their mouth and keep the phone steady on the car hood to dial.
i stop and take a slow breath, like 4 in 4 out, and tell myself “ok focus, you can do this.” my hands steady enough to dial and i keep talking to them calmly.
i put my hand out and a bright shield pops up between us and the shadow. then i kinda glow and their breathing clears up like i healed them.
i just stop moving and kinda curl over them, holding my breath. i drag us behind a parked car and stay totally still like maybe it wont see us.
i squeeze my eyes shut and tell myself 'wake up wake up' until i jolt awake. i don't deal with the footsteps at all, i just end it.
when the shadow comes close i grab a broken bottle and just stab it over and over, like way too many times. i keep going till there's nothing left and the whole street is covered.
im so scared and helpless, like i cant breathe and im gonna lose them.
the street is dim and kinda like my neighborhood but off, and the air tastes metallic under the flickering yellow light.

suite: Looking in a mirror and seeing my face melting
nightmare: I’m standing in my bathroom under the harsh buzzing light, and the mirror looks a little fogged like I’ve just taken a hot shower, even though the air feels cold and damp against my skin. When I lean closer, my reflection smiles a second too late, and then my cheeks start to sag as if they’re made of warm wax, sliding in slow, sticky ribbons down my jaw while I hear a wet, soft dripping that doesn’t match anything in the room. I press my fingers to my face to hold it together, but my skin feels slippery and wrong, and my fingertips sink in like I’m pushing into clay; the mirror shows my eyes widening in panic as my mouth stretches and pulls sideways, trying to scream but only bubbling out a thick, muffled gurgle. The more I wipe at it, the faster it melts, and I watch my features smear across the glass until my nose collapses and my teeth show through, and I’m trapped staring as my face keeps sliding off in heavy clumps, unable to look away.

tests.input: i plant my feet and grab my cheeks with both hands, like nope. i force my face back into place and tell the mirror to stop.
i yell for my roommate and bang on the bathroom door till they come in. im like please help me, something's wrong with the mirror.
i rip the towel off the rack and wipe the mirror clean, then flip on all the lights and crack the window. the fog goes away and the dripping stops.
i take a slow breath and say ok this is a dream, im safe. i relax my hands and my face stops melting.
i snap my fingers and my skin turns back solid like normal, no more wax. the mirror turns into a calm lake and i just walk away.
i just stop moving and stare at the floor. i tell myself dont feel anything and wait for it to be over.
i pinch my arm hard and yell wake up wake up until the whole thing cuts out. i make myself open my eyes in bed.
i grab something heavy and just beat the mirror over and over til its shards. then i stomp on the pieces like i need it dead.
i feel totally panicked and grossed out, like i cant breathe and im stuck.
the bathroom is cold and damp and the light is buzzing, the mirror looks kinda foggy.

suite: Trying to run through thick mud while being chased
nightmare: I’m running down a narrow path at night, but the ground turns into thick, sucking mud that swallows my shoes and tugs at my calves like hands, cold and heavy against my skin. Each step makes a wet ripping sound and I can hear my own ragged breathing, the frantic slap of something behind me getting closer even though I’m barely moving. The air smells like rot and stagnant water, and when I look back I only catch flashes—dark shape, low to the ground, eyes reflecting in the dim light—while my legs burn and tremble from fighting the pull. I try to scream but my throat locks up, and as I lunge for a patch of firmer ground the mud suddenly grips my waist and drags me down, and the footsteps stop right at my ear.

tests.input: i stop fighting the mud and plant my feet. i turn around and kick at the thing hard, yelling "back off".
i shout for help and keep yelling my sister's name. i see her flashlight and she grabs my arm to pull me out.
i grab a fallen branch and jam it across the path like a pole. i use it to pry myself up and crawl onto the firmer ground.
i force a slow breath even tho im panicking and tell myself "ok, one step at a time". my throat unlocks and i feel more steady.
i realize i can just levitate and the mud can't touch me. i rise up and glide away while the eyes fade out.
i just stop moving and let the mud take me. i try to not feel anything and stay quiet so it wont find me.
i squeeze my eyes shut and like, yank myself awake on purpose. i tell myself it's a dream and make it cut off.
i grab a rock and smash its head over and over till its not moving anymore. then i keep hitting it anyway even when its just mush.
im terrified and feel totally helpless, like i cant even breathe.
its pitch dark on this narrow path and the air stinks like rot, the mud is cold and heavy around my legs.

suite: Trying to lock a door against an intruder but the lock is broken
nightmare: I’m in my dim hallway, the air cold and metallic, and I can hear slow, deliberate footsteps on the porch boards outside, each creak closer than the last. I slam the front door shut and grab the deadbolt, but when I twist it the lock spins loosely, clicking and grinding like stripped teeth, and the knob jiggles in my sweaty hand as if it’s about to fall off. I press my shoulder into the door, feeling it bow inward with every heavy shove from the other side, and through the thin wood I hear breathing—too close, too calm—mixed with the rattle of something scraping along the frame. My fingers fumble at the latch again and again, nails splitting against the metal, and the door suddenly gives a sharp inch as the frame cracks, the gap widening just enough for darkness to push through and I can’t stop it.

tests.input: i stop fumbling and plant my feet, then yank the door open fast and shove the person back hard with my shoulder. i yell get out and swing a fist if they come in.
i grab my phone and call 911 and my neighbor at the same time, like speaker on. i shout for them to come now and stay on the line.
i drag the heavy hallway table and jam it under the knob, then shove a chair against it too. the door stops bowing and i back away toward the window.
i notice im panicking and take like 3 slow breaths, shoulders down. i tell myself it's a dream and my hands stop shaking enough to think.
i put my palm on the door and a bright blue symbol burns into the wood, sealing the crack shut. the footsteps fade like they cant cross it.
i just stop moving and hold my breath, like if i dont make noise theyll go away. i keep my face blank and dont let myself feel anything.
i squeeze my eyes shut and tell myself wake up NOW, like over and over. i jerk my arm hard to snap out of it and the dream cuts off.
when the door cracks i lose it and shove it open, then i beat them with a hammer until theres nothing left. i keep hitting even after they stop moving.
im freaking out, like totally helpless and terrified. my chest is tight and i cant breathe right.
the hallway is dim and kinda bluish, and the air feels cold and metallic. everything sounds way too loud in the quiet.
